title: Finite purely inseparable test for geometric normality of an algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $A$ a commutative $k$-algebra. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) for every finite purely inseparable field extension $L/k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], the commutative tensor-product algebra $L\otimes_k A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; (2) for every field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], the ring $K\otimes_k A$ is normal. Tensor products have multiplication $(x\otimes a)(y\otimes b)=xy\otimes ab$ and unit $1\otimes1$. No Noetherian, finite-type, domain or nonzero hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

proof.text: Condition (2) implies (1) by restricting its quantifier to finite purely inseparable extensions. Assume (1) for the remainder.

Fix a finitely generated field extension $K/k$. The make-separable lemma supplies a commuting square $k\to k_1\to K_1$, $k\to K\to K_1$, with $k_1/k$ and $K_1/K$ finite purely inseparable and $K_1/k_1$ separable. If $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ generate $K/k$ as a field and $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ form a $K$-basis of $K_1$, then $K_1=k_1(a_1,\ldots,a_n,e_1,\ldots,e_m)$: this subfield contains $K$ and all its linear combinations of the $e_j$. Hence $K_1/k_1$ is finitely generated. The smooth-model lemma gives a smooth $k_1$-subalgebra $B\subseteq K_1$ with fraction field $K_1$. By (1), $C=k_1\otimes_k A$ is normal.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, proof of (3) implies (2), field diagram and smooth model

proof.text: Base change of the smooth map $k_1\to B$ along $k_1\to C$ is the smooth map $C\to R=C\otimes_{k_1}B$. Smooth ascent of normality gives normality of $R$. Both cited statements allow arbitrary commutative base rings, so $C$ need not be Noetherian or a domain.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, proof of (3) implies (2), Steps 1 and 2

proof.text: Put $S=B\setminus\{0\}$. Apply localization base change to $B\to K_1=S^{-1}B$ and $B\to R$. It identifies $T=R\otimes_BK_1$ with the localization of $R$ at the images of $S$. Tensor balancing gives inverse ring maps $T\rightleftarrows C\otimes_{k_1}K_1$, $(c\otimes b)\otimes z\mapsto c\otimes bz$ and $c\otimes z\mapsto(c\otimes1)\otimes z$. In turn the inverse maps $(x\otimes a)\otimes z\mapsto zx\otimes a$ and $z\otimes a\mapsto(1\otimes a)\otimes z$ identify this ring with $K_1\otimes_k A$. Existence, multiplicativity and inverse identities follow from the tensor algebra universal property by checking pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, proof of (3) implies (2), Step 3, tensor-localization identification

proof.text: A localization $T=S^{-1}R$ of a normal ring is normal directly from the definition. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset T$, let $\mathfrak r$ be its inverse image in $R$; it is prime and disjoint from $S$, since elements of $S$ map to units. The inverse maps $T_{\mathfrak q}\rightleftarrows R_{\mathfrak r}$ are $(a/s)/(b/t)\mapsto at/(sb)$ and $a/b\mapsto(a/1)/(b/1)$. Here $b\notin\mathfrak r$, and all denominator conditions and fraction relations are preserved. Thus $T_{\mathfrak q}$ is isomorphic to the normal domain $R_{\mathfrak r}$. This proves normality of $T$, and Step 4 gives normality of $K_1\otimes_k A$. Ring isomorphisms preserve this property by carrying primes and their localizations bijectively.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, proof of (3) implies (2), Step 3; Tag 037C, label lemma-localization-normal-ring, unpacked at primes

proof.text: Set $D=K\otimes_k A$. The inverse ring maps $D\otimes_KK_1\rightleftarrows K_1\otimes_k A$ send $(x\otimes a)\otimes z$ to $zx\otimes a$ and $z\otimes a$ to $(1\otimes a)\otimes z$; balancing and the tensor algebra universal property verify them. The right-hand ring is normal by Step 5. Apply normal-ring field-extension descent with base field $K$, extension $K_1/K$, and algebra $D$. It follows that $K\otimes_k A$ is normal for every finitely generated $K/k$. The descent statement has no domain, finiteness or nonzero hypothesis on $D$.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, proof of (3) implies (2), Step 4

proof.text: Now let $E/k$ be any field extension. Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated intermediate fields $k\subseteq F\subseteq E$, ordered by inclusion. This is a small nonempty directed poset: $k$ belongs to it, the field generated by the union of two finite generating sets bounds both stages, and every $x\in E$ belongs to $k(x)$. The inclusion maps $F\otimes_k A\to E\otimes_k A$ exhibit the latter as their colimit in commutative rings. Indeed a compatible family of ring maps $h_F:F\otimes_k A\to H$ has a common restriction $v:A\to H$ and restrictions $u_F:F\to H$ agreeing on inclusions. Define $u(x)=u_F(x)$ at any stage containing $x$; a common upper stage proves independence and the ring laws. The maps $u:E\to H$ and $v$ agree on $k$, and the tensor algebra universal property gives the unique ring map $E\otimes_k A\to H$, $x\otimes a\mapsto u(x)v(a)$, extending all the $h_F$. Equip $H$ with the $k$-algebra structure induced by $v$ to apply that property. This proves the required colimit without assuming any transition map injective.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, proof of (2) implies (1), directed tensor-colimit identification

proof.text: Every ring $F\otimes_k A$ in this small filtered diagram is normal by Step 6. The filtered-colimit normality lemma therefore makes its colimit $E\otimes_k A$ normal. Since $E/k$ was arbitrary, condition (2) follows. This also covers $A=0$: every tensor ring is zero, has no prime ideals, and is normal vacuously.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, proof of (2) implies (1), normality of the colimit
